James Wynn Felizola is the founder of TERRAFORMS, an ecological land use planning and organic input materials consulting practice founded in 1993 in Eugene, Oregon.

His research and field work run from conservation subdivisions and on-site wastewater treatment in Appalachian Ohio to a hemp feasibility study for South Africa, with published papers, technical bulletins, and designs for gardens, orchards, greenhouses, and solar homes along the way.

[Bio]

James Wynn Felizola founded TERRAFORMS in Eugene, Oregon in 1993. The practice joins ecological land use planning with organic input materials consulting, and it is built on permaculture design: siting roads, water, and waste systems, and planting for food, energy, shade, and wildlife habitat.

The work has moved with him, from Eugene, Oregon to Athens, Ohio, to Rustenburg and Gauteng in South Africa, and now to Olympia, Washington. Along the way he co-founded the Belize Agroforestry Research Center and the Lost Valley Agroecology Internship Program, and wrote on conservation developments, sustainable agriculture, and ecological waste treatment.

Where land use planning meets the living site

Planning and design for conservation and natural recreation areas, residential lots and homes, mixed use commercial areas, roads, ponds, water supply, stormwater management, waste treatment, and plantings for food, energy, shade, and wildlife habitat.

BS in Environmental Science (Ecological Agriculture), The Evergreen State College, 1988. MS in Environmental Studies, Ohio University, 2008. Permaculture design courses, basic, advanced, and teachers, 1993. Twenty years of experience providing permaculture certified designs, consulting, teaching, research, and development.

“Expertise in the thoughtful and protracted observation of site characteristics to plan for optimal diversity and productivity.” [ TERRAFORMS, Consulting ]

TERRAFORMS owner James Wynn Felizola has published research on conservation developments, sustainable agriculture, and ecological waste treatment, including papers on on-site water supply and a feasibility report on hemp for South Africa.

His clients have ranged from the Athens Metropolitan Housing Authority and Community Food Initiatives in Ohio to the Southern Africa Hemp Company and organic input suppliers across North America and Europe.
